sources.location: scratchpad/PXD035899/raw-header-instruments.json; scratchpad/PXD035899/raw-header-proof.tsv (1 MiB range hashes and UTF-16LE model-string offsets)

claims.location: source name, comment[data file], characteristics[painting code] rows 1-15
claims.value: 11 painting acquisitions from ten named paintings A-J, plus four laboratory blanks
claims.evidence: Every RAW entry carries projectAccessions PXD035899. Filenames encode the painting letter and collection number, matching paper Table 1. J/KS114 occurs twice. Four files are named Blank_*.raw. The paper says laboratory blanks were processed alongside the canvas samples.

claims.location: characteristics[organism], characteristics[organism part], characteristics[sampled material] rows 1-15
claims.value: not applicable; painting ground layer and underlying canvas, or laboratory extraction blank
claims.evidence: The investigated sources are artwork composites rather than single-organism samples. Methods say ground layer and canvas were processed together and blanks monitored contamination. Species identified downstream were not used as input-sample organisms.

claims.value: Q Exactive HF for J_KS114_1226, J_KS114_1231, Blank_1227 and Blank_1232; Q Exactive HF-X for the remaining 11 runs
claims.evidence: Downloaded only bytes 0-1048575 of each accession-scoped public Thermo RAW file. The UTF-16LE instrument-model header explicitly says 'Q Exactive HF - Orbitrap MS' or 'Q Exactive HF-X - Orbitrap MS'. The paper's painting-level instrument prose differs for A,C,G,I; per-run RAW header is used for those files.

claims.location: comment[cleavage agent details] (two columns), comment[dissociation method], comment[collision energy], comment[precursor mass tolerance], comment[fragment mass tolerance] rows 1-15
claims.value: rLysC then Trypsin; HCD 28% NCE; 4.5 ppm precursor and 20 ppm fragment
claims.evidence: Methods report two-hour rLysC and overnight Trypsin digestion, HCD at 28% NCE, and the stated MaxQuant search tolerances.

claims.value: Fixed carbamidomethyl C; variable oxidation M and P, deamidation N/Q, Gln/Glu pyroglutamate, and protein N-terminal acetylation
claims.evidence: Methods list fixed carbamidomethyl, first-search variable modifications including hydroxyproline (encoded as oxidation P), and third-search N-terminal acetylation. Other third-search-specific glycation adducts are described in limitations because the paper does not give exact controlled terms and target sites.

limitations: The paper's instrument grouping differs from the deposited RAW instrument-model headers for A,C,G,I. The run-specific RAW headers take precedence. The deposited headers also resolve all four blank-run instruments.
The paper describes a pilot measurement for A, I and J, but the deposited filenames do not identify pilot runs. They are annotated by painting and instrument without an unsupported pilot/main label.
Painting J has two acquisitions from aliquots of the same extract. They are represented as technical replicates 1 and 2, not two biological specimens.

The third cereal/yeast database search also considered 3-deoxyglucosone condensation product, hexose and double-hexose additions, and N-terminal glycation. Exact controlled modification terms and target residues are not stated, so these are not encoded as NT/AC modification parameters.
The SDRF has no factor value because the study compares ten distinct paintings without a manipulated experimental factor.
